text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a geo sweep comparing p50/p95 across us-east / us-west / eu-west for the new 13B quantized bring-up (model: redwood/13b-q4_k_m). Edge routing toggled between 'nearest-pop' and 'balanced-cost'. Charts here: https://go/reports/geo-bench-1798004321

alex: Nice. What hardware did you test on? A100/H100/L4? Also what seq-len and concurrency?

sasha: Test matrix: A100-80GB and H100-80GB, seq=512, batching disabled for p50/p95 measurement, concurrent RPS sweep 50/200/1000 (per-region). Quantization: q4_k_m on both GPUs; we also ran q8_0 on H100 for throughput comparison.

maria: Numbers (median/p95) from the main run (H100, seq512, balanced-cost routing): us-east p50 44ms / p95 118ms; eu-west p50 49ms / p95 132ms; us-west p50 58ms / p95 276ms. When switching routing to nearest-pop (push traffic to west), us-west p95 jumps to ~320ms under burst.

alex: That's a big tail in us-west. Any kernel fallbacks or NVLINK cross-pop issues?

sasha: We saw a pattern where the fused-attn kernel (v2) sometimes falls back to a slower path on H100 for certain batch sizes when sequence distribution skewed. The fallback only triggered on the west-pop under load (we think because the west cluster has a slightly different CUDA/kernels build). Heap of logs show frequent: `WARN kernel_fallback: fused_attn_v2 -> fused_attn_generic` around the p95 spikes.

tim: Did you isolate networking vs runtime? Could be an edge-pop egress saturation or a routing ACL causing retries.

maria: Did both. We pinned to local GPU (bypassed gateway) and re-ran — tail persisted, so mostly runtime/kernel. But when we recompiled the runtime with updated kernel selection heuristics (branch mm-kernel-fix) the p95 in us-west dropped from ~320ms to ~150ms in a quick smoke. So kernel path was the dominant factor.

alex: Good find. Any quantization quality regressions observed after the kernel change?

sasha: No quality regressions in our eval suite (1000 prompts). Perplexity and exact-match stable. We did see a slight throughput improvement for q8_0 on H100 (2.2x vs q4_k_m in tokens/sec) but cost-wise q4_k_m still wins for token unit cost.

maria: Ops recommendations from the run:
- For now, set routing policy to `balanced-cost` with west as secondary for high QPS routes (avoid nearest-pop during bursts).
- Roll kernel patch mm-kernel-fix to west cluster; schedule canary on 5% traffic first.
- Update capacity sizing: assume 30% headroom for west due to observed tail — provision additional GPU pool (1 extra H100 per 2000 concurrent seq512 streams) until kernel patch lands.

alex: Can you paste the benchmark command and routing snippet? I'll open infra PR.

maria: Sure — benchmark command used:
```bash
./bench_geo --model redwood/13b-q4_k_m \n  --gpus H100 --seq 512 --concurrency 200 --duration 600 \n  --regions us-east,us-west,eu-west --edge-routing balanced-cost
```
Routing snippet we recommend adding to service config:
```yaml
routing:
  policy: balanced-cost
  region_preference:
    - us-east
    - eu-west
    - us-west   # deprioritized during QPS spikes
  fallback: any-compatible-quantized
```

tim: I'll schedule the canary and add observability hooks (trace sampling + token-level latency). infra-bot: create canary job?

infra-bot: Canary job created: canary-1798004321-mm-kernel-fix (5% traffic, duration 2h). Logs streaming: https://go/logs/canary-1798004321

sasha: I'll run the full A100/Ampere sweep tomorrow to see if any other clusters exhibit fallback behavior.

maria: Thanks — I'll file a short postmortem and attach the full charts + raw traces to the ticket. Action items: alex (infra PR), tim (canary + alert thresholds), sasha (A100 sweep), maria (postmortem + charts). :thumbsup:
